english.title: Dishonestly fail notify change of circumstances affecting entitlement to social security benefit / advantage / payment
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), dishonestly failed to promptly notify

(A)_[the Department for Work and Pensions]_
(B)_[a local authority, namely **(.. SPECIFY THE AUTHORITY..)]_

in the prescribed manner of a change of circumstances which you knew would affect your entitlement to **(..SPECIFY THE BENEFIT / ADVANTAGE / PAYMENT ENTITLED TO..), namely **(..SPECIFY THE CHANGE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 111A(1A) and (3) of the Social Security Administration Act 1992.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence inserted by Section 13 of the Social Security Administration (Fraud) Act 1997, as amended by the Child Support, Pensions and Social Security Act 2000, Schedule 6 to the Child Support, Pensions and Social Security Act 2000 and Schedule 6 to the Child Support, Pensions and Social Security Act 2001.
(ii) Section 111A(1A)(b) of the Social Security Administration Act 1992 provides that the change specified in above offence wording must NOT be a change excluded by regulations from those changes which must be notified.
(iii) For relevant social security legislation see Section 121DA of the Social Security Administration Act 1992.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
